sources: Luke 1:39-45, 56 (Mary rises and goes with haste into the hill country, to a city of Juda; enters the house of Zachary and salutes Elizabeth; when Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb; Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Ghost, cries out with a loud voice: “Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?”; Mary abode with her about three months). Douay-Rheims (Challoner).
Luke 1:36 (Elizabeth, Mary’s cousin, has conceived a son in her old age; Douay “cousin,” Greek syngenis, kinswoman). Luke 1:46-55 (the Magnificat: “My soul doth magnify the Lord”).
Luke 1:28 (“Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women”).

The Hail Mary: first half from Luke 1:28 and 1:42 with the names Mary and Jesus added; second half (“Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.”) added later by the Church. Catechism of the Catholic Church 2676-2677. On the rosary, ten Hail Marys in each decade.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? when you get big news, who’s the first person you want to tell?
options: then you already know how mary felt. listen.
someone who just gets it. that’s who mary ran to.
that’s okay. watch what happens when news gets shared.

steps.line: After the angel left, Mary hurried into the hill country to see her cousin Elizabeth. Elizabeth was old, and expecting a baby too.

steps.q: Mary walks in and says hello. What happens the moment Elizabeth hears her voice?
o: Elizabeth asks who told her the news
steps.why: The baby leaps. Before anyone explains anything, a tiny one already knows.

steps.line: Mary came in and greeted her. The moment Elizabeth heard Mary’s hello, the baby inside her leaped.

steps.q: The baby who leaps will be John the Baptist. Years later, what does he say when he sees Jesus coming?
o: “Here is the King of the Jews”
steps.why: John 1:29. The one who leaped before birth spends his life pointing to Jesus. Catholics hear his words at every Mass, just before communion.

steps.line: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Elizabeth cried out, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!”
“Why is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” Mary answered with a song of praise, and stayed about three months.
Today, Catholics join the two greetings, the angel’s and Elizabeth’s, into one prayer: the Hail Mary. Then they add a request: pray for us.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Half the Hail Mary is two greetings from Luke. The “pray for us sinners” half came much later. When was the whole prayer fixed in its final form?
steps.why: The two greetings were prayed for centuries. The request grew in the late Middle Ages, and the full prayer was set in the Church’s prayer book of 1568.

steps.q: The second half of the Hail Mary asks, “Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us.” Why ask Mary to pray, instead of just praying to God?
o: She can answer prayers in God’s place
Only saints could speak to God directly
Like asking a friend to pray for you
steps.why: Catholics aren’t asking Mary to take God’s place. They’re asking her to pray alongside them, now and at the very end.

say: here’s what i love. half the hail mary is just two hellos from luke: an angel’s and a cousin’s. the church set them side by side and added two names, mary and jesus.
then the prayer turns and asks: holy mary, mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. on the rosary it comes ten times in a row, like a heartbeat.

steps.q: Elizabeth is greeting Mary, but she calls her “the mother of my Lord,” and her own baby leaps. Who is all the joy really about?
o: Mary, the young cousin who traveled so far
steps.why: Elizabeth calls him “my Lord” before he is even born, and her own baby leaps for him. That’s why the Hail Mary’s greeting ends with his name: Jesus.

today.say: once today, read the hail mary slowly, one breath per line. you can just read it, learn it, or pray it. notice where the hellos end and the asking begins.
options: slow is how you hear the hellos turn into asking.
that counts. reading it is how most people first met it.
